name: Input Buffer
description: Input assist for Geometry Dash: early clicks are buffered, late clicks can still use an orb or jump off a ledge, flying inputs are evened out, and an experimental lookahead simulates the next moments to shift, block or save clicks. Shows an on-screen counter of every click it changed.

sec-general.name: General
sec-general.description: Master switch, safety and display. Everything below can be changed while paused (pause menu, **Buffer** button).

enabled.name: Buffer Enabled
enabled.description:
Master switch for everything this mod does.

Hotkey: **F5** (shows a small popup).

practice-only.name: Practice Mode Only
practice-only.description:
When on, the buffer only works while practice mode is on. In normal mode every click goes straight to the game, so you can't upload a completion or progress with the buffer helping by accident.

Turn it off only for unrated or offline levels.

show-overlay.name: Show Overlay
show-overlay.description:
Shows a label in the bottom-left corner with the active settings and how many clicks the mod changed this attempt. It flashes when it helps:

**Green** = early click saved
**Orange** = late orb rescued
**Cyan** = late jump off a ledge
**Yellow** = click shifted by Lookahead
**Red** = click blocked by Lookahead
**Purple** = Auto Save

**Adj** counts flying inputs whose timing was evened out. **Total** counts every rescue since you opened the level.

tps.name: Game Speed (TPS)
tps.description:
**Auto** (recommended) reads the speed from the game itself. The overlay shows the value it found; on an unmodified game it should say **240 auto**. If it shows something else, pick your real TPS here instead.

Otherwise this must match the TPS you set in Mega Hack, or 240 if you have not changed it.

The mod uses this to turn ticks into real time. It does not change your game's speed.

guide.name: How to read the timing numbers
guide.description:
Timing windows are measured in **ticks**. A tick is one tiny step of the game's physics. There are 240 ticks per second, so:

**1 tick** = about 4 milliseconds
**2 ticks** = about 8 ms
**4 ticks** = about 17 ms (1 frame at 60 FPS)
**8 ticks** = about 33 ms (2 frames)
**16 ticks** = about 67 ms (4 frames)
**32 ticks** = about 133 ms (8 frames)

On every window setting:
**-1** = use the Main Buffer Window
**0** = off, raw input with no help
**1 or more** = your own value

Smaller windows are stricter and feel more natural. Larger windows are more forgiving but can fire clicks earlier or later than you meant.

sec-ground.name: Landing and orb modes
sec-ground.description:
Cube, ball, robot and spider.

These windows set how long before landing or touching an orb a click is still remembered. If you tap a little early and let go, the click fires the moment you touch the ground or orb.

stage.name: Main Buffer Window
stage.description:
The default window for every mode that is set to -1 below.

**2 ticks** = about half a frame (very strict)
**4 ticks** = about 1 frame (a good starting point)
**8 ticks** = about 2 frames
**16 ticks** = about 4 frames (very forgiving)
**32 ticks** = about 8 frames (extreme)
**Off** = no default window

A bigger window is more forgiving, but a click meant for later might fire sooner than you wanted.

cube-ticks.name: Cube Window (ticks)
cube-ticks.description:
How early you can click before landing or touching an orb in cube and still have it count.

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window
**0** = off
**1 or more** = your own value

Examples: 4 = about 1 frame early, 8 = about 2 frames early, 16 = about 4 frames early.

ball-ticks.name: Ball Window (ticks)
ball-ticks.description:
How early you can click before touching a surface or orb in ball and still have it count.

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window
**0** = off
**1 or more** = your own value

Examples: 4 = about 1 frame early, 8 = about 2 frames early, 16 = about 4 frames early.

robot-ticks.name: Robot Window (ticks)
robot-ticks.description:
How early you can click before landing or touching an orb in robot and still have it count.

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window
**0** = off
**1 or more** = your own value

Examples: 4 = about 1 frame early, 8 = about 2 frames early, 16 = about 4 frames early.

spider-ticks.name: Spider Window (ticks)
spider-ticks.description:
How early you can click before touching a surface or orb in spider and still have it count.

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window
**0** = off
**1 or more** = your own value

Examples: 4 = about 1 frame early, 8 = about 2 frames early, 16 = about 4 frames early.

hold-refire.name: Re-press Held Clicks
hold-refire.description:
Ball and spider don't react to a button that is already held when they land. With this on, an early click you are still holding is released and pressed again on landing, so it still flips or teleports.

Cube and robot jump on their own when you land holding, so they don't need it.

sec-late.name: Late clicks
sec-late.description:
The early buffer helps when you click **too early**. These help when you click **too late**:

**Late orb**: you passed an orb without using it and click right after. The orb fires anyway, from where you are now.

**Late jump**: you ran off the edge of a block and click right after ("coyote time"). You still jump, flip or teleport as if you clicked on the edge.

Neither applies to wave, or while you are on the ground.

late-orb-ticks.name: Late Orb Window (ticks)
late-orb-ticks.description:
How long after leaving an unused orb a click still fires it.

**0** = off
**4** = about 1 frame late (default)
**8** = about 2 frames late
**16** = about 4 frames late

Big values can fire an orb you meant to skip, if you click soon after it for something else.

coyote-ticks.name: Late Jump Window (ticks)
coyote-ticks.description:
How long after running off a ledge a click still jumps (cube, robot), flips (ball) or teleports (spider).

**0** = off
**4** = about 1 frame late (default)
**8** = about 2 frames late
**16** = about 4 frames late

Only counts when you ran off the edge. Leaving the ground with a jump, pad or orb never gives a second jump.

sec-fly.name: Flying modes
sec-fly.description:
Ship, UFO, swing and wave.

There is no ground to wait for here, so these windows work differently. In ship, UFO and swing, a very quick tap is made to last at least this long, so fast taps come out the same length every time. In wave, the window is used by the Wave Mode you pick.

When **Lookahead** is on, it takes over flying-mode timing and these styles are skipped.

ship-ticks.name: Ship Window (ticks)
ship-ticks.description:
The shortest a tap can be in ship. A quicker tap is stretched to this length.

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window
**0** = off, raw input
**1 or more** = your own value

Examples: 2 = taps last at least about half a frame, 4 = at least about 1 frame.

Bigger values can make quick taps feel slower or heavier.

ufo-ticks.name: UFO Window (ticks)
ufo-ticks.description:
The shortest a tap can be in UFO. A quicker tap is stretched to this length.

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window
**0** = off, raw input
**1 or more** = your own value

Examples: 2 = taps last at least about half a frame, 4 = at least about 1 frame.

Bigger values can make quick taps feel slower or heavier.

swing-ticks.name: Swing Window (ticks)
swing-ticks.description:
The shortest a tap can be in swing. A quicker tap is stretched to this length.

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window
**0** = off, raw input
**1 or more** = your own value

Examples: 2 = taps last at least about half a frame, 4 = at least about 1 frame.

Bigger values can make quick taps feel slower or heavier.

wave-ticks.name: Wave Window (ticks)
wave-ticks.description:
How strong the wave timing help is. The meaning depends on the Wave Mode below:

**Min Hold**: the shortest a tap can be
**Min Gap**: the shortest wait between letting go and pressing again
**Grid**: the size of the timing grid (every click and release waits for the next grid line)

**-1** = same as Main Buffer Window, but never more than 8 ticks
**0** = off, raw input
**1 or more** = your own value (not capped)

2 or 4 is a good place to start. Large values make wave more consistent but much less responsive, and can feel very laggy.

wave-mode.name: Wave Mode
wave-mode.description:
Picks how the wave timing help works. The Wave Window above sets how strong it is.

**Min Hold**: a very short tap is stretched to at least the window length. Good if your quick taps come out too short or uneven.
Watch out: quick taps feel slightly longer than you pressed, and fast spam can feel sticky.

**Min Gap**: after you let go, the next press has to wait a minimum time. Good for fast zigzags that bunch up.
Watch out: a press that comes too soon is delayed, which can feel like a late or skipped click.

**Grid**: every press and release waits for the next beat of a fixed timing grid, so everything lines up evenly. Gives the most consistent result.
Watch out: adds a small delay to every click and release, up to the window size. It can feel laggy with large windows.

Switching modes in the middle of a wave section can cause one odd click, so change it while paused.

sec-lookahead.name: Lookahead (experimental)
sec-lookahead.description:
Lookahead runs invisible copies of your icon through the game's own physics a fraction of a second ahead, to see whether a click would crash before it happens.

It stops predicting at orbs, pads and portals (the path after them depends on what you do there), so near those it simply doesn't interfere.

It costs CPU: the overlay shows how many simulated steps per second it uses. Lower the lookahead lengths if the game stutters.

**Experimental:** it uses game internals that could only be checked against the game's code, not played. If something misbehaves, turn it off with **F11** and tell me what happened.

lookahead.name: Lookahead
lookahead.description:
Turns all Lookahead features on or off.

Hotkey: **F11** (shows a small popup).

smart-shift.name: Smart Shift
smart-shift.description:
When a click (or a release in ship, wave and robot) would crash, it is delayed to the first moment within the shift window that survives.

This is the natural-feeling one: you still make every click, the mod only nudges it a few milliseconds later.

shift-ticks.name: Shift Window (ticks)
shift-ticks.description:
How far Smart Shift may delay a click.

**4** = about 1 frame
**8** = about 2 frames (default)
**16** = about 4 frames

Bigger windows save more clicks but can make inputs feel late.

death-guard.name: Death Guard
death-guard.description:
When no shift saves a click but **not** clicking survives, the click is ignored.

In ship, wave and robot, a press or release you make is held back until it becomes safe, then goes through on its own.

auto-save.name: Auto Save
auto-save.description:
The extreme one: when what you are doing now would crash and the opposite input survives, the mod clicks (or lets go) for you.

Tap modes get a single tap at the last safe moment. Ship, wave and robot switch to the safe input and give control back as soon as your own input is safe again.

This plays parts of the level for you, so it does not feel natural. Off by default.

lookahead-ticks.name: Jump Lookahead (ticks)
lookahead-ticks.description:
How far ahead to simulate a jump in cube, ball, robot and spider. It stops early once the icon lands.

**96** = 0.4 s (default, covers a normal jump)
**48** = cheaper, sees less
**160** = long jumps and low gravity

hold-lookahead-ticks.name: Flying Lookahead (ticks)
hold-lookahead-ticks.description:
How far ahead to simulate ship, wave, UFO and swing. You keep steering in these modes, so a short look is enough.

**16** = about 4 frames (default)
**8** = tighter, cheaper
**32** = sees walls earlier, but may intervene more often

sec-keys.name: Hotkeys
sec-keys.description: Keys that work while you are in a level. Pick **None** to disable one. If two actions share a key, both will trigger. Hotkeys only work while the Geometry Dash window is focused.

key-toggle.name: Key: Buffer On/Off
key-toggle.description: Turns the whole mod on or off.

key-stage.name: Key: Cycle Main Window
key-stage.description: Steps the Main Buffer Window through 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 ticks and Off.

key-tps-up.name: Key: TPS Up
key-tps-up.description: Moves the Game Speed (TPS) setting up one preset (Auto, then 60, 120, 240...). Remember it must match your real TPS.

key-tps-down.name: Key: TPS Down
key-tps-down.description: Moves the Game Speed (TPS) setting down one preset. Going below 60 switches back to Auto.

key-debug.name: Key: Debug Logging
key-debug.description: Turns debug logging on or off.

key-wave.name: Key: Cycle Wave Mode
key-wave.description: Switches between Min Hold, Min Gap and Grid. Best used while paused.

debug.name: Debug Logging
debug.description: Prints detailed messages to the console about what the buffer is doing. Only useful for troubleshooting. Leave it off for normal play.
